newsitem.title: USA: L.A. County warns of cost of prenatal aid cutoff.
newsitem.headline: L.A. County warns of cost of prenatal aid cutoff.

text.p: The elimination of prenatal care for undocumented immigrants in Los Angeles County could cost California taxpayers more than $20 million a year, according to a county report to be released on Wednesday.
The Los Angeles County Department of Health Services report warns that hundreds of babies would be born with severe long-term health problems, increasing state costs.
The report also warns that thousands of cases of untreated communicable diseases would occur in pregnant women, and communicable disease control would be seriously compromised.
Details of the report will be released at a press conference with representatives from the Los Angeles County Department of Health Services on Wednesday.
In response to federal welfare reform, California Gov. Pete Wilson is moving quickly to eliminate prenatal care for undocumented immigrants.
The Wilson administration said it hopes to use the money spent on illegal immigrants to expand prenatal care services to low-income legal residents and citizens.
